purpose: Qualitative demand/friction intelligence for people who become sick for a longer period while participating in an Arbetsförmedlingen programme. Scores are not measured search volumes and do not prove eligibility. Natural problem formulations are discovery signals; current Arbetsförmedlingen and Försäkringskassan primary sources carry the truth-bearing transition rules.

scoring.priority_rule: Prioritize combinations of high demand, high friction, high consequence and weak current product coverage; these scores are not measured search volumes.

natural_language_queries: jag går i program med aktivitetsstöd och har varit sjuk över 30 dagar vad händer nu
arbetsförmedlingen program sjuk mer än 30 dagar sjukpenning
jag är fortfarande i programmet men har varit helt sjuk länge ska jag söka sjukpenning
jag blev utskriven ur arbetsförmedlingens program efter lång sjukdom vad gör jag dagen efter

demand_signal.basis: Arbetsförmedlingen and Försäkringskassan both maintain dedicated current guidance for sickness during labour-market programmes, including the >30-day boundary. This is a qualitative national reach proxy, not measured search volume.

friction_signal.basis: Users can easily collapse three different facts into one: sickness duration, full-time versus partial sickness and whether Arbetsförmedlingen has actually ended the programme. Only the actual status change makes the post-programme sickness-benefit route relevant.

miss_consequence.basis: An automatic switch based only on 30 days can send a person to the wrong authority too early, while missing an actual programme exit can delay a time-sensitive sickness-benefit application and the correct medical-certificate route.

source_fragmentation.basis: Arbetsförmedlingen explains programme absence, adaptation and programme exit, while Försäkringskassan separately explains the sickness-benefit route after the programme has been ended.

language_accessibility_friction.basis: Terms such as heltidssjuk, programdeltagare, utskriven, läkarintyg and sjukpenning describe different transition states and are easy to interpret as an automatic 30-day rule.

steps_to_action.basis: The useful path is short but conditional: stay on the programme sickness route, consider adaptation, establish whether full-time sickness exceeded 30 days, verify whether the programme was actually ended, and only then use the post-programme Försäkringskassan route.

recurrence_signal.basis: Both agencies keep current dedicated guidance for the boundary and Arbetsförmedlingen explicitly publishes a subsection for sickness longer than 30 days, indicating a durable recurring information need.

current_product_coverage_gap.basis: The shared v47 route correctly handled first-day reporting and the seven-day medical-certificate boundary but stopped before the >30-day full-time transition and therefore could not distinguish still-enrolled from actually-written-out users.

signals.recommended_learning_action: Extend the existing unemployed_sick route instead of creating a new matcher. Keep the normal programme route immediate; expose the >30-day branch only when relevant. Distinguish full-time sickness from partial sickness and actual programme exit from duration. Only after confirmed programme exit point to the Försäkringskassan post-programme application route, while preserving separate eligibility assessment.
signals.truth_rule: VERIFY the >30-day transition against current Arbetsförmedlingen and Försäkringskassan primary sources. Do not treat 30 days alone as automatic programme exit, do not apply the full-time transition to partial sickness, and do not turn an actual programme exit into a guarantee of sickness-benefit eligibility.
